Fat from Potato Chips Virtual Lab

Extraction of Fat from Potato Chips - CHM-125L Lab 9

Purpose

By the end of this lab you will be able to:

  • Extract the fat from a weighed sample of potato chips using hexane
  • Calculate the percent fat in the chips from your own measurements
  • Calculate the % fat stated on the nutrition label and compare it with your result using percent error

Student Information

Your answers are saved in this browser as you work, so you can close the page and come back. Turn in the downloaded PDF on Canvas by Monday 11/30.

Background

Why hexane pulls the fat out of chips

Background Information

Fats are organic compounds made of long hydrocarbon chains, so they are nonpolar.

Hexane (C6H14) is also nonpolar. Because "like dissolves like," fat dissolves easily in hexane. (Ligroin and petroleum ether work the same way.)

Hexane boils at about 69 °C, so a gentle hot plate evaporates it and leaves the fat behind in the beaker.

The whole lab in one line
chips + hexane → filter out the chip pieces → evaporate the hexane → only fat is left → weigh the fat

Key Equations

Mass of fat = (mass of beaker + fat) − (mass of empty beaker)
% Fat in chips = (mass of fat ÷ mass of chips) × 100
Reported % fat = (total fat per serving ÷ serving size in grams) × 100
% Error = (experimental % fat − reported % fat) ÷ reported % fat × 100
